newsitem.title: USA: Calif. tax measure may hurt muni utilities - S&P.
newsitem.headline: Calif. tax measure may hurt muni utilities - S&P.

text.p: Standard & Poor's Corp warned on Tuesday that a California tax measure approved by voters last November could hurt the ratings of some municipal utilities in the state.

California's Proposition 218 requires that local taxes be submitted to voters for approval. Under the proposition, many local governments and agencies may be required to reduce or repeal existing property-related fees and assessments that do not meet the measure's restrictions.
S&P said in its CreditWeek Municipal newsletter that it is not yet clear how the tax measure's provisions apply to water, sewer and solid waste collection fees.
If the proposition is found to control utility fees, S&P warned that there could be impacts from rate rollbacks. S&P said ratings could also be affected if challenges to utility fees become common.
Some utilities may be more vulnerable under Proposition 218 than others, S&P said.

The rating agency said it generally views utilities that have high rates, need substantial rate increases for capital requirements and have a history of political opposition to rate increases as weaker credits.
